title: Configure the router WAN and LAN interfaces
prompt: A small office is replacing its router. Assign each address and mask to the correct interface using the provider handoff and office plan. Keep the public handoff separate from the private LAN.
briefing: Provider handoff: documentation network 198.51.100.12/30; usable addresses .13 and .14; .13 is the ISP gateway and .14 is assigned to this router. The required WAN mask is 255.255.255.252.
Office LAN: 172.22.16.0/24 with mask 255.255.255.0. The router must use .1. A client already uses .20; do not duplicate it.
Enter the router WAN address, WAN mask, WAN default gateway, LAN address and LAN mask. These public documentation addresses are fictional training values; no real router is changed.
explanation: Use the provider-assigned .14 address and /30 mask on the WAN with .13 as its next hop. Use 172.22.16.1/24 on the LAN. The client address .20 is already occupied, and the LAN address is not the ISP-side gateway. The ticket supplies the subnet boundaries so there is no vendor syntax or subnet-size guesswork.
reference:
Ports: WAN connects to ISP handoff; LAN connects to office switch.
Draft configuration has the WAN and LAN addresses reversed.

title: Repair the media archive parity array
prompt: A four-member RAID 6 archive array has one failed member. Inspect the simulated controller, choose a replacement that meets both interface and capacity requirements, then rebuild safely.
briefing: The array has four 8 TB SATA members. A verified backup is available and the enclosure supports the approved hot-replacement procedure.
Shelf stock: SN-T500 is 6 TB SATA; SN-T600 is 8 TB SAS; SN-T700 is 8 TB SATA and is controller-approved. This enclosure accepts SATA replacement members only.
Type help for the fictional training commands. Inspect raid status and raid drives, identify the failed serial, replace it with the compatible spare, then run raid rebuild.
RAID 6 protects against two member failures, but do not remove a healthy member or treat redundancy as a backup.
explanation: The failed member is SN-T202 in bay 2. Use raid status, raid identify SN-T202, raid replace SN-T202 SN-T700, and raid rebuild. SN-T500 lacks capacity and SN-T600 has an unsupported interface. Preserve healthy members and verify the simulated rebuild reaches OPTIMAL.
reference: The controller inventory, not the order of spare labels, identifies the failed disk and suitable replacement.

raid_config.degraded_detail: One failed member; parity redundancy is reduced.

title: Prepare a contractor mobile connection
prompt: Complete five independent parts of a contractor phone setup using the device capabilities and approved company workflow.
briefing: This phone has a physical SIM tray and does not support eSIM. The carrier supplied an activated compatible physical SIM.
The car hands-free system and phone both display pairing code 627194. The supplied procedure says to confirm matching codes on both devices before testing a call.
The contractor is joining the company BYOD program. Policy requires its approved work-profile enrollment while retaining personal applications.
New business contacts must synchronize to the company account, not remain in device-only storage. The company account already supports contact synchronization.
An approved laptop needs internet through the phone. No USB cable is available, both devices support Wi-Fi, and the plan permits hotspot use.

options.label: Fit the supplied compatible physical SIM as documented
Load an eSIM despite missing device support
Treat a Wi-Fi password as a SIM profile
Confirm the matching codes, then test a call
Ignore the code mismatch check and pair with any listed device
Enroll in the approved company work-profile workflow
Use only a personal file-sync account
Configure the approved Wi-Fi hotspot and connect the laptop
Use USB tethering without a cable
Use an NFC tap as the continuing internet link

explanation: Use the supported physical SIM, verify matching pairing codes and test audio, follow the approved BYOD work-profile enrollment, store contacts in the synchronized company account and use the permitted Wi-Fi hotspot. Each selection respects the stated hardware and company constraints.
reference: Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, account credentials and carrier coverage have already been tested. Follow the ticket rather than factory-resetting a working phone.

title: Calculate guest allocations from worker counts
prompt: Allocate resources to three VMs from their approved workload formulas and storage policies. The host has 16 vCPU and 64 GiB available to guests after overhead, and overcommit is prohibited.
briefing: Database simulator: three workers, each requiring 2 vCPU and 8 GiB. Allocate their combined resources to its one VM; use the low-latency datastore.
Remote client simulator: two workers, each requiring 2 vCPU and 6 GiB. Allocate their combined resources to its one VM; use the capacity datastore.
Web test VM: exactly 2 vCPU and 12 GiB; use the capacity datastore.
Catalog: /volumes/ssd-runtime = low-latency runtime storage; /volumes/hdd-runtime = capacity runtime storage; /volumes/exports = export files only. All have sufficient free space.
CPU/RAM totals above either host limit lose all CPU/RAM credit. Storage placements remain independently scored.
explanation: The database needs 3 × (2 vCPU, 8 GiB) = 6 vCPU/24 GiB. The client simulator needs 2 × (2 vCPU, 6 GiB) = 4 vCPU/12 GiB. Add 2 vCPU/12 GiB for the web VM: 12 vCPU and 48 GiB total. Put the database on SSD runtime and the other two on capacity runtime; exports is not an active datastore.
reference: Worker requirements are additive within each VM. Do not create extra VMs or allocate per-worker values as the VM total.

title: Interpret a power-rail diagnostic
prompt: A desktop halts during startup. Use its supplied service legend and the technician measurements to identify the failing subsystem and appropriate repair.
briefing: Fictional model Northstar P8 reports code P7. Its service legend defines P7 as an out-of-range supply rail, M2 as memory training failure and B4 as missing boot media.

A qualified technician tested the disconnected PSU using the manufacturer-approved fixture. The +12 V output measured 8.7 V; the supplied acceptable range is 11.4–12.6 V. The fixture was verified against a known-good unit.
Use the provided measurements; you are not being asked to probe a live PSU. A correctly rated compatible replacement supply is available.
Choose the faulty subsystem and corrective action. Do not open the PSU enclosure or defeat the power protection.

options.label: Isolate power, replace the PSU with the approved compatible unit and verify stable operation
Open the PSU enclosure and attempt an internal repair

explanation: P7 and the independently confirmed 8.7 V reading identify an out-of-range PSU output. Isolate power and replace the supply with an approved compatible unit, then verify stability. RAM, storage and display replacement do not correct the demonstrated supply fault; internal PSU repair is outside this service task.
reference:
Diagnostic display: P7
Measured +12 V rail: 8.7 V
Specified service range: 11.4–12.6 V
Test fixture: verified

title: Explain touch behavior with gloves
prompt: A tablet responds normally to bare fingers, but ordinary thick work gloves do not register touches. The screen is undamaged and the model has no glove mode. What is the most appropriate recommendation?

options.text: Factory-reset the tablet before checking supported input accessories
Change mobile carrier settings to improve touch sensitivity
Replace the digitizer despite reliable bare-finger input
Use a supported input accessory or compatible touchscreen gloves approved for the device and work environment

explanation: Some capacitive touchscreens do not detect ordinary insulating gloves. Normal bare-finger response argues against replacing the digitizer based only on this evidence. Use compatible input equipment suited to the working conditions.

title: Reduce scan file size for ordinary text
prompt: An MFD is producing unnecessarily large files when scanning ordinary monochrome text at very high color resolution. Which setting change best matches the workflow while retaining required readability?

options.text: Select an appropriate text/grayscale or monochrome mode and sufficient, lower resolution
Change the fax dial tone detection only
Enable print duplexing without changing scan settings
Increase color bit depth and resolution for every page

explanation: Choose scan mode and resolution to meet the document purpose. Ordinary text often does not need very high color resolution, which increases file size. Print duplexing and fax dialing do not change scan image encoding or resolution.

title: Connect a temporary survey camp
prompt: A survey camp has no wired service or terrestrial mobile coverage but can install a terminal with the provider-required view of the sky. Which access technology is the most suitable?

options.text: DSL without a provider telephone access line
Satellite internet
A point-to-point Bluetooth link with no upstream service
Cable broadband without a provider coaxial connection

explanation: Satellite can provide an internet access path where terrestrial services are unavailable, subject to coverage and installation requirements. A local Bluetooth link does not supply an upstream service, and DSL/cable require their respective provider connections.

title: Investigate a persistent display outline
prompt: An OLED display shows the faint outline of a static status panel even when other content is shown. The outline remains in the display own test image with the source disconnected. What is the most likely category of fault?

options.text: A source video-driver fault that cannot appear in the monitor internal test
A damaged cable still controlling the image after the source is disconnected
Panel image retention or burn-in
An incorrect workstation resolution that changes the monitor internal test image

explanation: The outline persists in the monitor internal test even with the source disconnected, implicating panel retention or burn-in rather than the source driver, cable or desktop resolution. Follow the manufacturer guidance to determine whether retention is temporary and what service options apply.

title: Validate signed outbound messages
prompt: A mail system adds a domain-associated digital signature to outbound messages. Receiving servers use a published DNS public key to verify it. Which mechanism is being used?

options.text: DKIM
A DHCP reservation
SPF alone
An MX priority value

explanation: DKIM uses domain-associated signatures and published public keys for message verification. SPF evaluates authorized sending sources instead; MX priorities guide inbound delivery, and DHCP reservations assign addresses.

title: Replace thermal pads on an expansion card
prompt: A vendor service procedure specifies thermal pads of particular thicknesses on memory chips and paste on the GPU die. Which TWO actions should the technician take?

options.text: Use the specified pad thickness and placement for each contact
Substitute a thick stack of random pads everywhere
Apply the documented thermal material for each surface
Omit the pads because the card fans still spin
Assume thermal paste can bridge every pad-sized gap

explanation: Thermal contact depends on the intended material, thickness and mounting pressure. Follow the service specification for each surface. Fans cannot compensate for missing contact, and paste should not be assumed to fill a designed pad gap.

title: Restore an approved business app
prompt: A managed phone lost access to a corporate app after its management enrollment was removed. Personal internet access still works. Which TWO actions are appropriate under the company procedure?

options.text: Disable all organizational controls to make the app launch
Re-enroll the device using the authorized company management workflow
Verify that the required managed app and policy are reassigned after enrollment
Change the personal email account password as the only repair
Install an unapproved copy from an unrelated download site

explanation: Restore authorized management and verify the app assignment rather than bypassing policy. Working personal internet access does not restore management enrollment. A personal mailbox password does not assign the corporate application.

title: Understand a static configuration
prompt: A printer has a manually configured static IPv4 address. The DHCP server is temporarily unavailable, but the printer, client, switch and route remain operational. Which statement is correct?

options.text: The printer must change to a random public address immediately
A static address forces the printer to use DHCP for every print job
The printer must lose its configured subnet mask when DHCP stops
The printer does not need a new DHCP lease merely to continue using its valid manual configuration

explanation: A manual static configuration is not leased from DHCP. Its continued operation still depends on valid addressing and connectivity, but DHCP unavailability alone does not erase those settings or require a new lease.

title: Find an exhausted PoE budget
prompt: Several access points work from a PoE switch. A newly added unit receives no power, but works alone on a verified compatible injector. The switch reports that its total PoE budget is exhausted. Which TWO actions are appropriate?

options.text: Replace all access point radio antennas
Compare total device demand with the switch available PoE budget
Provide approved additional power capacity or move suitable loads to another supported source
Change only the access point DNS server
Increase every port requested power beyond the switch capacity

explanation: The reported aggregate power limit and successful injector test point to budget capacity. Verify demand and provide a supported power arrangement. DNS and antennas do not increase available PoE power, and allocating beyond the budget does not create capacity.

title: Identify a directory lookup service
prompt: A support tool queries a directory using its standard unencrypted LDAP service. Which destination port is associated with that service?
explanation: LDAP conventionally uses port 389. SMB, RDP and POP3 use the other listed ports for different purposes. This identifies the service; it does not recommend sending sensitive directory traffic without appropriate protection.

title: Compare wireless bands
prompt: All else being equal, a client and access point can use either 2.4 GHz or 5 GHz. Which TWO considerations are reasonable when choosing a band?

options.text: 5 GHz always reaches farther through every material
Using 5 GHz makes interference and regulatory limits irrelevant
2.4 GHz often penetrates obstructions better in typical indoor layouts
2.4 GHz cannot carry IP traffic
5 GHz commonly offers more channel-planning options than 2.4 GHz

explanation: Band choice trades propagation and available spectrum among other factors. Actual performance depends on power, antennas, interference and the building. No band makes interference, regulation or environmental testing unnecessary.

title: Use a virtual machine for another operating system
prompt: A support engineer must run a Linux-only diagnostic alongside the existing desktop OS without rebooting between them. Which approach meets the requirement?

options.text: Change the host boot order without installing a guest runtime
Run a supported Linux guest VM on the desktop hypervisor
Use ordinary dual boot with one active OS at a time
Rename the executable to match the host file extension

explanation: A supported guest VM can run the required OS concurrently with the host. Ordinary dual boot requires selecting one booted OS at a time. Renaming an executable or changing display input does not provide an OS runtime.

title: Choose a routed destination
prompt: A PC at 10.8.3.22/24 needs to contact 10.8.9.40. Its configured gateway 10.8.3.1 provides the required route. Which IP next hop should it use?

options.text: 10.8.9.40 as an assumed on-link neighbor despite the /24 mask

explanation: The destination lies outside the PC local /24 subnet, so the PC sends the traffic toward its configured gateway. Loopback addresses the local host, and the subnet broadcast is not the unicast next hop for this routed destination.

title: Interpret a CPU support list
prompt: A system fails POST immediately after a CPU upgrade. The socket matches, but the board CPU-support list requires a newer firmware revision for this processor. What should the technician do?

options.text: Format the system disk before addressing firmware support
Assume matching sockets guarantee support and replace the monitor
Follow the supported firmware-update or recovery procedure using the required compatible hardware
Force a different memory generation into the slots

explanation: Socket fit alone does not guarantee firmware support. Use the board documented update procedure, which may require the previous CPU or a supported recovery feature. Disk formatting and unrelated display replacement do not add processor initialization support.

title: Connect a serial management port
prompt: A legacy device specifies a nine-pin DB9 serial management connection with vendor-specified serial signaling. Which accessory is appropriate for a laptop with only USB?

options.text: A passive VGA display cable chosen because it has a D-shaped shell
A USB-C charging adapter with no data interface
A USB-to-Ethernet adapter without serial support
A compatible USB-to-serial adapter and the correct serial cable/pinout

explanation: Use an adapter providing the required serial interface and matching pinout/signaling. Connector-shell resemblance does not establish compatibility. Ethernet and power-only adapters do not provide a DB9 serial management interface.

title: Replace a motherboard in a compact chassis
prompt: A technician selects a microATX motherboard for an existing compact case. Which TWO checks directly establish installation suitability?

options.text: The case supports that motherboard form factor and mounting positions
Use case color as proof of CPU socket compatibility
The power, rear I/O and required expansion clearances match the planned build
Assume every full ATX board fits a microATX-only enclosure
Support the board by its cables instead of the documented standoffs

explanation: Match the supported form factor, standoffs, interfaces and clearances before installation. Larger boards do not necessarily fit compact cases, and cables must not substitute for mounting hardware. Color does not establish electrical or socket compatibility.

title: Connect a legacy mobile accessory
prompt: A handheld device has a documented microUSB data socket. A technician has a USB-C host laptop and must connect the device for synchronization. Which cable meets the need?

options.text: A data-capable cable or supported adapter path matching USB-C at the host and microUSB at the device
A miniUSB cable forced into the microUSB socket
A USB-C-to-USB-C cable with no adapter
A microUSB charge-only cable

explanation: Match both connector types and data capability. MiniUSB and microUSB are different connector shapes, and charge-only cabling cannot carry synchronization data. Never force a mismatched connector.

title: Check DNS over a reliable transport
prompt: A DNS exchange requires TCP rather than UDP. Which destination port is still normally used by the DNS server?
explanation: DNS can use TCP as well as UDP on port 53. Changing transport does not change the standard service port to a DHCP, POP3 or SMB port. Both transports may need appropriate network policy support.

title: Identify the drum preparation stage
prompt: In a laser printer cycle, a component applies a uniform electrical charge to the drum before the laser forms the image. Which stage is described?

options.text: Charging
Cleaning residual toner after transfer
Paper separation
Fusing

explanation: Charging establishes the drum electrical condition before exposure. Fusing bonds toner to paper later in the process, paper separation is a media-handling step, and cleaning removes residual material rather than applying the initial uniform charge.

title: Respond to a suspected PSU electrical fault
prompt: A desktop emits a burning smell and a crackling sound from the power-supply area. What is the appropriate immediate response?

options.text: Shut down and disconnect power safely, then arrange replacement or qualified service without opening the PSU
Disable the PSU fan to reduce the noise
Open the PSU enclosure and touch components to find the hot part
Keep running a stress test to see whether the smell clears

explanation: Treat signs of an electrical fault as a reason to stop use and isolate power safely. PSU internals can retain hazardous energy; they are not a routine field repair for this task. Continued load or disabling cooling does not address the fault.

title: Place an outbound web intermediary
prompt: An organization routes browser requests through a host that fetches resources on behalf of clients and applies an access policy. Which server role is described?

options.text: DHCP server
Proxy server
Print server
NTP server

explanation: A proxy intermediates requests on behalf of clients and can apply configured policy. Time synchronization, address leasing and print queues do not describe the web-request intermediary.

title: Specify display color coverage
prompt: A designer compares monitors for a workflow that requires a documented color space. Which specification most directly indicates the range of colors the monitor can reproduce relative to that requirement?

options.text: Color gamut coverage
Refresh rate alone
Native pixel count alone
Screen diagonal alone

explanation: Color gamut describes a reproducible color range, often stated as coverage of a named color space. Refresh rate, physical size and USB connectivity do not establish that range. Calibration and accuracy remain additional considerations.

title: Align a replacement ink cartridge
prompt: After a supported ink-cartridge replacement, an inkjet printer produces offset vertical lines. The manufacturer provides an alignment utility for this symptom. What maintenance action should be performed?

options.text: Replace the paper pickup rollers before alignment
Change the queue destination address
Run only a scan calibration without aligning the ink placement
Run the documented printhead/cartridge alignment procedure

explanation: The symptom and supplied maintenance procedure point to alignment. Feed rollers address paper transport, network lease timing does not align ink placement, and an inkjet does not use a laser fuser.

title: Calculate single-parity capacity
prompt: An array uses five equal 2 TB disks in RAID 5. Ignoring formatting and controller overhead, what usable capacity does its single distributed-parity layout provide?

options.text: 8 TB
6 TB
2 TB
10 TB

explanation: RAID 5 dedicates the equivalent of one member capacity to distributed parity. With five equal 2 TB disks, usable capacity is (5 − 1) × 2 = 8 TB before overhead. This redundancy does not replace a backup.

title: Distinguish latency from bandwidth
prompt: A remote office has acceptable large-file throughput but noticeable interaction delay over its geostationary satellite link. Round-trip latency is consistently high even without congestion. Which explanation best fits?

options.text: The long satellite signal path adds propagation delay that more local Wi-Fi bandwidth alone cannot remove
Increase an idle local LAN link speed and assume satellite propagation delay disappears
Blame DNS alone for sustained high round-trip delay to a known IP address
Assume acceptable file-transfer throughput rules out latency problems

explanation: Throughput and latency measure different properties. A long geostationary satellite path adds substantial propagation delay even when there is enough bandwidth. Upgrading an unrelated local component cannot remove that path delay.

title: Check guest resource requirements
prompt: A user wants to run two guest operating systems while keeping the host responsive. Which planning step is most appropriate?

options.text: Assign all physical RAM to guests and reserve nothing for host overhead
Plan solely from virtual disk capacity without checking CPU or RAM
Budget guest memory and CPU needs while reserving resources for the host and hypervisor
Treat virtual cores as additional physical cores created by software

explanation: Guest allocations consume host resources, and the host/hypervisor also needs capacity. Overcommit depends on workload and platform behavior rather than creating physical capacity. Resource planning should be based on actual requirements.

title: Choose NAT for a training guest
prompt: A lab VM needs outbound internet access through its host but should not be directly published to the office LAN by default. Which TWO statements describe a suitable NAT configuration?

options.text: The virtual NAT service translates guest traffic through an upstream address
NAT makes malware inside a guest harmless in all circumstances
Unsolicited inbound access generally needs an explicit forwarding arrangement
The guest must share every host storage volume automatically
The guest receives a dedicated public address without an upstream allocation

explanation: NAT can provide outbound connectivity using address translation. Inbound publishing usually requires explicit forwarding or another supported arrangement. NAT does not automatically share disks, grant public addresses or guarantee complete workload safety.

title: Connect a remote worker privately
prompt: An employee must access approved internal resources from a home network using the company VPN. Which TWO statements are correct?

options.text: Authorization to particular internal resources still applies after the tunnel connects
A VPN eliminates the need for a local IP address
Connecting any VPN automatically grants access to every internal system
The VPN can provide an authenticated encrypted tunnel over the existing internet connection
A VPN guarantees the home internet connection can never fail

explanation: A properly configured VPN protects and authenticates a tunnel, but access policies still determine resource permissions. It depends on underlying connectivity and does not guarantee availability or universal authorization.

title: Separate a container from a full guest OS
prompt: A team packages an application with its dependencies in an operating-system container. Which distinction should a support technician understand?

options.text: Containers guarantee compatibility with every host kernel
A container always requires a dedicated physical server
The container generally shares a host kernel rather than booting a complete independent guest kernel for each container
Every container boots a full independent guest kernel

explanation: Operating-system containers typically share a host kernel, unlike full VMs with their own guest kernels. Compatibility and isolation still depend on the platform. Packaging an application does not make it universally compatible with every kernel.

title: Recognize a community cloud
prompt: Several independent research organizations share cloud infrastructure restricted to their consortium and designed around common governance needs. Which deployment model best fits?

options.text: Community cloud
Public cloud offered broadly to unrelated customers
A single organization's local-only virtualization host without cloud services
Private cloud reserved for one organization

explanation: A community cloud serves a defined community of organizations with shared requirements. This differs from exclusive single-organization private cloud and broadly available public cloud.

title: Match a short-range radio use
prompt: A wireless mouse communicates with its paired laptop across a desk without joining the office IP WLAN. Which technology is the best fit among these choices?

options.text: Bluetooth
NTP server
DHCP server
DNS authoritative server

explanation: Bluetooth supports short-range peripheral communication without requiring the mouse to join the IP WLAN. DSL and satellite are access technologies, and twisted-pair Ethernet is a wired network medium.

title: Use a motherboard lane-sharing note
prompt: After an M.2 drive is installed, one existing SATA drive disappears. The board manual states that using this M.2 socket disables SATA port 2, where that drive is attached. What is the best correction?

options.text: Move the SATA cable to an available enabled port listed in the manual
Disable all storage controllers
Replace the SATA drive solely because it disappeared
Format the undetected SATA drive

explanation: The documented resource-sharing rule explains the missing device. Use a compatible enabled port and verify detection. Formatting or replacing the drive does not change the motherboard port-sharing design.

title: Choose the contacts account
prompt: A user wants newly created business contacts to appear on both a managed phone and the company web address book. The phone currently saves new contacts to device-only storage. What should be changed?

options.text: Set the company synchronized account as the default destination for new contacts
Disable company contact synchronization
Continue creating device-only contacts and assume all accounts share them
Change the default account only for outgoing mail

explanation: New contacts must be created in the synchronized business account to appear in that account elsewhere. Device-only and SIM storage are separate destinations; changing a ringtone does not change where contacts are stored.

title: Use a repeating-defect chart
prompt: A laser print has a mark repeating every 94 mm. The supplied service chart lists drum circumference 94 mm and fuser roller circumference 63 mm. What component should be investigated first?

options.text: The scan feeder pickup roller
The fuser roller despite its different documented circumference
The imaging drum assembly
The printer Ethernet cable

explanation: The repeated spacing matches the documented drum circumference, pointing to a defect recurring once per drum rotation. The fuser interval differs. Network transfer and the scan feeder do not create that print-engine periodic mark.

title: Locate a job sent to the wrong queue
prompt: A user reports missing output, but the job history shows successful delivery to a different floor printer selected in the application. What is the best correction?

options.text: Reinstall toner in the intended printer
Select the intended printer queue and confirm the default/application selection for future jobs
Change the intended printer address at random
Restart the intended printer without changing the selected queue

explanation: The job went to the selected destination successfully. Correct the application or default queue choice and verify the new job destination. Imaging consumables and unrelated hardware changes do not redirect a job sent to another queue.

title: Avoid damage during microphone service
prompt: A laptop has a replaceable internal microphone connected by a fragile flex cable. Which handling practice is appropriate during service?

options.text: Isolate power and release the documented connector before removing the microphone assembly
Leave the internal battery connected while shorting connector pins to test them
Fold the cable sharply to make room under a screw
Pull on the flex cable until the connector releases

explanation: Use the documented connector release and isolate power before service. Pulling a flex cable, sharp folds and pin shorting can damage the microphone, connector or board. The service manual determines the correct disassembly order.

title: Observe packets without a host agent
prompt: A network team needs an approved device placed in a wired link to provide a monitoring system with a copy of link traffic. Which tool is intended for this role?

options.text: Modular-plug crimper
Copper cable stripper
Tone probe
Network tap

explanation: A network tap provides a traffic observation point for monitoring. Crimpers, tone probes and strippers are cabling tools rather than packet-copying devices. Installation and monitoring must follow the approved network procedure.

title: Correlate intermittent wireless interference
prompt: A 2.4 GHz wireless link loses packets only when nearby interfering equipment operates. Wired clients remain stable. What should the technician evaluate first?

options.text: The local radio environment and a supported cleaner channel or band
Replace the stable wired uplink without checking the affected radio band
Reinstall every client OS before surveying interference
Expand the DHCP pool without investigating radio conditions

explanation: The correlation and stable wired traffic point to radio interference. Survey the environment and test suitable channel/band or placement changes. Address-pool size and printer settings do not remove RF interference; a wholesale reinstall ignores the observed cause.

title: Survey channel use
prompt: Before adjusting access points, a technician needs to see nearby wireless networks, their channels and received signal levels. Which tool most directly supplies this information?

options.text: RJ45 crimper
Ethernet loopback plug
Wi-Fi analyzer
Punchdown tool

explanation: A Wi-Fi analyzer presents radio-network observations useful for channel and coverage planning. The other tools install or test wired connections and do not list neighboring wireless channels.

title: Check a liquid-cooling pump fault
prompt: A desktop with an all-in-one liquid cooler rapidly overheats. Radiator fans spin, but the pump reports zero speed and its documented power connector is disconnected after service. What should be done?

options.text: Raise CPU voltage instead of powering the pump
Disable thermal shutdown because the radiator fans spin
Replace system memory before reconnecting the pump
Shut down, restore the correct pump connection according to the cooler instructions, and verify circulation and temperatures

explanation: Spinning radiator fans do not establish coolant circulation. Correct the disconnected pump power path with the system safely shut down and verify operation afterward. Raising CPU voltage, replacing RAM or defeating thermal protection does not power the disconnected pump.

title: Remove an accidental network loop
prompt: A small network becomes unusable just after a second redundant cable is added between unmanaged switches without loop prevention. Link LEDs show unusually heavy activity. Which TWO actions are appropriate?

options.text: Disconnect the newly added redundant connection under the approved recovery procedure
Flush DNS caches without changing the looped topology
Add another unmanaged redundant cable
Increase DHCP lease duration without removing the loop
Verify traffic and connectivity recover, then use a topology with appropriate loop prevention

explanation: The new unmanaged redundant path can create a Layer 2 loop and excessive traffic. Remove the accidental path and verify recovery, then design redundancy with suitable loop prevention. DNS and lease durations do not stop circulating Ethernet frames.

title: Check a biometric replacement
prompt: A technician must replace a laptop palm-rest assembly containing a fingerprint reader. Which check is most important when ordering the assembly?

options.text: Match only the case color and ignore reader compatibility
Confirm support for the exact laptop model and its fingerprint-reader connection
Choose any palm rest with the same overall width
Choose a keyboard-only assembly and assume it includes the fingerprint sensor

explanation: Physical dimensions or color alone do not establish electrical and mechanical compatibility. A biometric assembly must match the model and connection requirements; follow any manufacturer setup requirements after installation.

title: Plan an ECC upgrade
prompt: A technician wants error-correcting memory in a workstation. Which prerequisite matters beyond simply buying an ECC-labeled module?

options.text: Any motherboard accepting the connector must support active ECC
The processor, motherboard and firmware must support the intended ECC configuration
ECC works solely because the OS is 64-bit
An ECC module enables correction even if the CPU memory controller lacks support

explanation: ECC operation depends on platform support, not only the memory label or physical fit. Check CPU, board, firmware and supported module specifications. Display connections and USB storage do not enable memory error correction.

title: Recognize self-service provisioning
prompt: An authorized developer provisions an approved cloud test server through a portal without waiting for a provider employee to install it manually. Which cloud characteristic is illustrated?

options.text: Resource provisioning requiring manual provider installation for every request
Multitenancy alone, without considering how resources are provisioned
On-demand self-service
Metered billing alone, without any provisioning interface

explanation: On-demand self-service allows an authorized consumer to provision available resources through a defined service interface. It can still be subject to quotas, policies and billing; it does not imply unrestricted authority.

title: Separate positioning from map downloads
prompt: A field tablet has downloaded the needed maps and has a working GPS receiver. Cellular service is unavailable. Which statement correctly describes its ability to obtain a position?

options.text: Downloaded maps guarantee a satellite fix inside every building
It can obtain satellite-based position with adequate sky visibility even though online map updates are unavailable
GPS always requires an active cellular subscription to determine any position
Bluetooth pairing with a keyboard replaces the GPS satellite signal

explanation: GPS positioning and online map retrieval are different functions. A receiver can obtain satellite position without cellular service, although obstructions and acquisition conditions matter. Offline maps do not guarantee reception, and a Bluetooth keyboard is not a positioning source.

title: Select a headset for a wired call station
prompt: A laptop has a combined 3.5 mm headset jack. The user needs both headphones and a microphone on one plug. Which accessory should be selected?

options.text: A headset with the compatible combined audio/microphone plug for that jack
An optical digital-audio cable with no analog headset adapter
Headphones with a stereo-only plug and no microphone
A microphone-only cable with no headphone connection

explanation: The headset must support both audio directions using the combination jack wiring. A stereo-only plug does not add a microphone channel, and an optical cable is a different interface. Verify the laptop-supported pin arrangement.

title: Match removable storage support
prompt: A field camera supports SDXC cards only up to the capacity and speed class listed in its manual. What should determine the replacement card choice?

options.text: The largest-capacity card available regardless of device support
Any microSD card without a compatible physical adapter
A card matching the documented type, capacity limit and required speed class
A card selected solely by the color of its label

explanation: Removable-media compatibility includes format/type, capacity, physical fit and required performance. Bigger is not automatically supported. An adapter may address physical fit but does not guarantee support for the card capacity or standard.

title: Check CPU architecture for an application
prompt: A vendor supplies an application build specifically for ARM64 and another for x64. Why should a technician identify the computer processor architecture before installation?

options.text: Matching processor core counts guarantee binary compatibility
Changing firmware boot order translates one instruction set into another
All ARM64 binaries are native x64 binaries under another name
The installer must target an architecture the platform can run, directly or through explicitly supported compatibility mechanisms

explanation: ARM64 and x64 identify different instruction-set targets. Select a supported build and verify any supported compatibility layer rather than assuming native interchangeability. Case dimensions and display settings do not change the processor instruction set.

title: Enable an approved USB boot device
prompt: A technician has an authorized signed recovery USB device, but the computer firmware has external USB boot disabled. The device is detected normally by another PC. What setting should be reviewed first?

options.text: Change the SATA data cable to permit USB boot
The firmware USB boot permission and boot selection for the approved device
Replace the detected USB device immediately without reviewing firmware settings
Change only the OS desktop boot menu after the external boot failure

explanation: The known firmware restriction prevents the approved external boot path. Review the documented USB boot permission and select the device under the authorized service procedure. Unrelated display, printer or address settings do not enable firmware USB boot.

title: Recognize transport behavior
prompt: Which TWO statements correctly distinguish TCP and UDP for an application designer?

options.text: TCP provides an ordered byte stream with retransmission mechanisms
UDP does not itself guarantee packet delivery or order
UDP itself retransmits every missing datagram until acknowledged
UDP always encrypts datagrams automatically
TCP and UDP require the same connection handshake

explanation: TCP provides stream ordering and recovery mechanisms; UDP is a datagram transport without those guarantees. Encryption belongs to other mechanisms, and neither transport guarantees a particular end-to-end latency for every application.

title: Preserve operation after a PSU failure
prompt: A server has two hot-swappable 800 W power supplies in a supported redundant configuration. What must be true for one unit to carry the load after the other fails?

options.text: Both units must be disconnected at the same time for failover
The running load must fit within the supported capacity of one 800 W unit
The server may draw 1600 W continuously and still survive either supply failing
The redundant configuration makes power-source availability irrelevant

explanation: Redundancy requires the remaining supply to support the load under the platform specifications. Two units do not provide fault-tolerant 1600 W service when one 800 W unit must carry everything. Independent power paths can also matter for availability.

title: Inspect a new toner cartridge installation
prompt: Immediately after fitting a new laser-printer toner cartridge, pages are blank. The documented shipping seal is still in place on the cartridge. What should be done?

options.text: Restart the print server while leaving the cartridge seal in place
Remove the seal and reinstall the cartridge following the manufacturer instructions
Replace the network cable before correcting the cartridge installation
Increase scan resolution without removing the seal

explanation: Remove the documented shipping seal so toner can enter the print process, then reinstall and test as specified. Spooler restarts, cable replacement and scan settings leave the demonstrated cartridge installation fault unresolved.

title: Investigate a short after a case swap
prompt: A motherboard works on an approved insulated service bench but will not power on when mounted in a replacement case. Which TWO installation checks are most relevant?

options.text: Increase voltage to overcome suspected conductive contact
Check for an extra metal standoff contacting the board underside
Reinstall the operating system before examining mounting
Check for trapped conductive debris or an incorrectly positioned I/O shield tab
Replace the boot drive that worked on the bench

explanation: The change with mounting suggests a case-related short or contact. Inspect standoffs, debris and shield placement with power isolated using the service procedure. Software networking and higher voltage do not correct a physical short.

title: Respect per-slot memory limits
prompt: A board supports a maximum of 64 GB RAM across four slots, with at most 16 GB per supported module. Which configuration satisfies both documented limits?

options.text: One 64 GB module in the first slot
Two 32 GB modules solely because they total 64 GB
Four 32 GB modules with half the capacity disabled in the OS
Four supported 16 GB modules

explanation: Four supported 16 GB modules meet both the total and per-module limits. A matching total alone does not make larger unsupported modules valid. The operating system cannot be assumed to correct unsupported memory population.

title: Inspect an unreliable charging connection
prompt: Several verified charging cables fit loosely in a phone port. With the phone powered off, a technician sees packed lint preventing full insertion. What is the best next action?

options.text: Probe energized contacts with a metal pin
Follow the manufacturer-approved port inspection and cleaning procedure without damaging the contacts
Replace the battery before addressing the visible obstruction
Force the connector into the obstruction

explanation: Debris prevents proper seating and can explain the loose connection. Use the approved safe cleaning method, avoiding force and conductive probing. A battery replacement does not remove the physical port obstruction.

title: Track department printing
prompt: A shared multifunction printer supports authenticated usage tracking. Which TWO configurations help attribute print usage to the correct departments?

options.text: Change only the default paper tray by department
Configure the supported user or department accounting identifiers
Use the same anonymous identifier for every department
Disable device accounting after enabling authentication
Verify that the queue or device records jobs against those identifiers

explanation: Supported accounting identifiers and recorded job attribution allow usage tracking by department. Anonymous shared identities obscure attribution; paper color alone does not create reliable electronic accounting. Verify support in the actual device and print workflow.

title: Check optical-media compatibility
prompt: A department archives files on rewritable Blu-ray media. Which TWO specifications should be verified for the planned drive?

options.text: Support for the selected disc capacity and format
Choose a CD-ROM-only drive because the discs have a similar diameter
Assume read-only Blu-ray support guarantees rewriting
Support for writing the selected BD-RE media type
Ignore capacity differences within the supported media family

explanation: Reading, writing and rewriting are distinct capabilities, and disc types/capacities must be supported. A CD-ROM drive is not a Blu-ray writer. Check the drive/media compatibility specifications rather than physical appearance.

title: Interpret a Mini-LED display specification
prompt: A monitor is advertised as an LCD with Mini-LED local-dimming backlighting. Which statement correctly distinguishes it from an OLED display?

options.text: Mini-LED alone guarantees the panel native resolution
The LCD requires no light source behind its image layer
Its LCD layer modulates light from a backlight rather than every image pixel being an OLED emitter
Each Mini-LED LCD pixel is necessarily an OLED emitter

explanation: Mini-LED describes a backlight implementation used with LCD panels, often with many dimming zones. OLED image pixels emit their own light. Neither term alone fixes the panel resolution, refresh rate or connector specification.

title: Assign patching responsibility
prompt: A team rents basic cloud virtual machines and controls the guest operating systems. Under this IaaS arrangement, who normally patches those guest operating systems unless a separate managed service is purchased?

options.text: No party needs to patch a guest OS once it is virtualized
The public internet transit provider patches the cloud guest OS
The customer team responsible for the guests
The infrastructure provider automatically patches every guest OS under basic IaaS

explanation: In a basic IaaS arrangement, the provider manages the underlying infrastructure while the customer manages guest operating systems. Managed services can change the division, so the service agreement matters. IaaS alone does not imply automatic guest patching.

title: Separate Wi-Fi association from network authorization
prompt: A visitor joins the approved guest SSID and obtains an address, but internet browsing redirects to the guest registration page. Other registered visitors have access. What should the technician check?

options.text: Disable guest access controls for all users
Replace the radio adapter despite successful association and normal registration redirects
Whether the visitor has completed the authorized guest access workflow
Change to random static addresses to bypass registration

explanation: Association and DHCP configuration do not necessarily complete guest-network authorization. The expected registration page is evidence of a captive-portal workflow. Use the approved access process rather than bypassing controls or creating address conflicts.

title: Distinguish cloud file sync from a backup policy
prompt: A business uses cloud file synchronization across devices. Which TWO points should shape its data-protection plan?

options.text: Required recovery history and retention must be verified separately
Every sync product guarantees unlimited immutable history
A synchronized deletion can propagate to other devices
Synchronization eliminates the need to test restoration
Any synced folder remains recoverable forever after account deletion

explanation: Sync keeps working copies aligned and may propagate deletions. Recovery depends on the service retention/version features and the backup policy, so verify and test them. Cloud synchronization alone does not guarantee indefinite recoverability.

title: Select managed switching features
prompt: A branch must place different switch ports into assigned VLANs and inspect interface error counters remotely. Which TWO characteristics should be required?

options.text: Management access to the relevant port status and counters
An unmanaged switch selected solely by port count
A passive patch panel with no active management
A basic repeater without VLAN support or counters
A managed switch supporting the needed VLAN configuration

explanation: Managed switching provides configuration and operational visibility when those features are supported. An unmanaged switch or passive panel cannot be assumed to offer VLAN administration or remotely readable per-port counters.

title: Build a straight-through copper patch lead
prompt: A technician is terminating a conventional straight-through four-pair Ethernet patch lead. Which termination choice is appropriate?

options.text: Put all conductors of the same color family on one pin
Use the same approved T568A or T568B pin assignment at both ends
Use T568A on one end and T568B on the other and label it straight-through
Use random pair placement as long as all eight pins are present

explanation: A straight-through lead uses the same standard pin assignment on both ends. T568A-to-T568B is a crossover arrangement for the relevant pairs, not the requested straight-through wiring. Preserving pair assignments matters, not merely connecting eight conductors.

title: Replace a damaged camera module
prompt: A laptop camera has a cracked lens. The display and microphone work, and the service manual lists a replaceable camera module behind the bezel. What is the best repair approach?

options.text: Replace the complete motherboard before inspecting the replaceable module
Install a higher-resolution module solely because its connector looks similar
Remove the cracked lens and leave the module exposed
Use the specified camera module and follow the documented bezel and cable service procedure

explanation: Use the supported part and model-specific procedure to protect the display, cables and enclosure. A similar connector does not establish compatibility. The identified replaceable component does not justify replacing an otherwise working motherboard.

title: Choose a managed application runtime
prompt: Developers need to deploy code to a managed runtime while the provider manages the runtime platform and underlying OS. Which service model best fits?

options.text: Basic IaaS with customer-managed guest operating systems
A finished SaaS product with no code-deployment platform
An unmanaged physical server rented without a managed runtime
PaaS

explanation: PaaS supplies a managed platform for application deployment. Basic IaaS leaves more OS responsibility with the customer, while a finished SaaS product is consumed as an application rather than used as the stated runtime platform.

title: Resolve exhausted storage capacity
prompt: An imaging workstation cannot save new files. Its data volume is healthy but has no free space, and an approved archive target is available. What is the best response?

options.text: Move or remove approved data according to retention policy and verify enough free space
Replace the SATA data cable as the only response
Defragment the healthy full volume and assume that creates additional free capacity
Suppress the low-space warning without moving or removing data

explanation: The healthy but full volume needs approved data moved or removed, or appropriate capacity added under the retention policy. Defragmentation reorganizes existing data and is not a substitute for freeing capacity. A replacement cable or hidden alert does not create free space.

title: Diagnose unreadable printer output
prompt: A printer produces its internal test page correctly. Jobs from one newly installed workstation contain garbled symbols; other workstations print normally. The affected workstation uses a driver for a different printer language. What should be corrected?

options.text: Install the appropriate driver or supported page-description-language configuration
Clean the paper pickup rollers
Replace the printer drum immediately
Replace every toner cartridge

explanation: A working internal page and other clients narrow the fault to the affected client print configuration. An incompatible driver or page-description language can produce garbled output. Imaging consumables and feed rollers do not translate the wrong job language.

title: Move print processing to a server
prompt: An office wants a central place to queue jobs, share printer access and administer network print queues for multiple clients. Which host role is appropriate?

options.text: Mail relay
Print server
NTP server
DNS secondary server

explanation: A print server centralizes print queues and related administration. Time service, name resolution and mail relay have different functions. The printer and client environment still require suitable drivers and access permissions.

title: Scan a stack of originals
prompt: An office needs to scan many loose, uniform pages without placing each sheet on the glass by hand. Which feature most directly supports this workflow?

options.text: Automatic document feeder
An output stapler alone
A second toner cartridge
A print-only duplex unit with no scanning feeder

explanation: An ADF feeds originals through the scanner. Output finishing and toner relate to printed output, and a print duplexer alone does not feed scan originals. Check whether duplex scanning is also required for two-sided originals.

title: Select a dual-SIM data line
prompt: A supported phone has a business SIM and a travel eSIM. Both are active, but only the travel line includes the approved local data allowance. What should the technician configure?

options.text: Select the travel line for cellular data and prevent automatic fallback to the other data line if the device supports that control
Choose the business line for all data despite its missing local allowance
Leave automatic data switching enabled without checking its fallback behavior
Change the Wi-Fi SSID instead of choosing the cellular data line

explanation: On a supported dual-SIM device, the data line can be selected independently of other line preferences. Select the authorized plan and review fallback behavior so data does not unexpectedly use the other subscription. Exact menus depend on the device.

title: Follow an FTP control connection
prompt: A packet capture shows a client establishing the standard FTP control session before requesting a file. Which destination TCP port normally carries that control connection?
explanation: FTP control commands normally use TCP 21. TCP 20 is associated with the server data connection in active FTP, while data-channel behavior differs by mode. DNS and IMAP use other services and ports.

title: Understand a patch-panel role
prompt: A rack has horizontal copper runs terminated on a patch panel and short patch cords leading to switch ports. What does the patch panel primarily provide?

options.text: Layer 3 routing between the connected subnets
Wireless authentication for nearby clients
Automatic DHCP leases for every wall jack
An organized passive termination and cross-connection point

explanation: A conventional patch panel provides passive structured-cabling termination. The connected active equipment performs switching, routing and services. A patch panel does not itself assign addresses or authenticate wireless clients.

title: Recognize a desktop PSU output
prompt: A desktop PSU receives mains AC. What does it normally provide to internal components?

options.text: Alternating mains input voltage unchanged at each motherboard connector
Only one universal DC voltage for every internal connection
A voltage determined solely by the monitor refresh rate
Regulated DC outputs such as 3.3 V, 5 V and 12 V

explanation: A desktop PSU converts AC input into regulated DC rails used by the system. It does not send unconverted mains voltage to ordinary motherboard power pins. Address leasing and optical signaling are unrelated to its power-conversion role.

title: Troubleshoot one unreadable optical disc
prompt: An optical drive reads several verified discs of the supported format, but fails on one visibly scratched disc. What is the most appropriate initial conclusion?

options.text: The SATA controller must be replaced immediately
The entire workstation RAM capacity is insufficient to read any disc
All supported optical formats have become incompatible
The particular disc is the leading suspect; use the approved cleaning or replacement process

explanation: Successful reads of comparable supported discs isolate the issue toward the damaged medium. Follow handling guidance and replace or recover the disc as appropriate. The evidence does not justify replacing the storage controller or blaming total system RAM.

title: Interpret performance during an array rebuild
prompt: A RAID array is rebuilding after an approved disk replacement. The controller reports steady progress, no additional failed members and slower application disk response. What is the best initial action?

options.text: Monitor rebuild health and progress and manage the workload according to the maintenance plan
Cancel the rebuild and initialize every member
Declare the replacement defective solely because response is slower during rebuilding
Remove another healthy drive to speed recovery

explanation: Rebuilding uses storage resources and can reduce application performance. With healthy progress and no new fault evidence, monitor and manage load under the maintenance plan. Destructive initialization or removing a healthy disk creates unnecessary risk.

title: Use a supported docking power budget
prompt: A laptop requires a documented 90 W USB-C Power Delivery input for normal operation under load. A dock provides only 45 W to its host port. Which replacement specification addresses this limitation?

options.text: A compatible dock and cable that deliver at least the required 90 W to the host
A dock with more USB ports but the same 45 W host limit
A passive connector adapter that changes plug shape without increasing delivered power
A dock advertising 100 W total power while explicitly limiting its host output to 45 W

explanation: Check the power delivered to the laptop, not total dock input or the number of ports. The dock, cable and laptop must support the required negotiated power. A passive shape adapter cannot create additional power.

title: Recognize an industrial control network
prompt: A factory uses networked systems to supervise production equipment and collect measurements from industrial controllers. Which category most closely describes this environment?

options.text: An email relay serving only mail transfer
An ordinary consumer file-synchronization folder
A print-server spool queue
SCADA

explanation: SCADA describes supervisory control and data acquisition in industrial environments. Such systems may have specialized availability and maintenance requirements; they are not simply print queues or passive cabling.

title: Choose cable for an air-handling space
prompt: A project specification requires communications cable approved for the building plenum air-handling space. Which selection satisfies the stated requirement?

options.text: Cable with the specified plenum fire/smoke rating
Any outdoor direct-burial cable, regardless of its indoor rating
A higher category number alone, without the specified fire rating
Any unmarked cable with the desired connector

explanation: The specified plenum rating addresses flame and smoke characteristics for that installation environment. Category/performance and outdoor protection are separate attributes. Follow the project specification and applicable installation requirements rather than assuming one rating implies another.

title: Identify thermal-transfer supplies
prompt: A label printer uses heat to transfer material from a ribbon onto label stock. Which consumable is directly involved in forming the printed image?

options.text: Only heat-sensitive direct-thermal paper with no ribbon
A laser toner drum
A liquid-ink reservoir in a separate inkjet printhead
The compatible thermal-transfer ribbon

explanation: Thermal-transfer printing uses a ribbon to deposit material on the media. Direct thermal printing uses heat-sensitive media without a transfer ribbon. Laser and inkjet consumables are different printing mechanisms.

title: Identify a dedicated storage network
prompt: Several servers access shared block-storage devices through a purpose-built network fabric dedicated to storage traffic. Which network type is described?

options.text: A public guest WLAN
PAN
SAN
A single-host loopback

explanation: A storage area network provides networked block-storage access to hosts. A personal-area or guest wireless network does not describe this dedicated storage fabric. A file share and a block-storage fabric should not be treated as identical services.

title: Publish authorized mail senders
prompt: A domain owner wants to publish a DNS policy listing systems permitted to send email for that domain. Which mechanism best matches this purpose?

options.text: Automatic DHCP leasing on wall jacks
SPF in a DNS TXT record
Layer 3 routing between the connected subnets
Active frame switching based on learned MAC addresses

explanation: SPF publishes authorized sending sources through DNS TXT data. MX selects inbound mail destinations; it does not list the allowed outbound senders. Address records and DHCP exclusions serve other purposes.

title: Respond to liquid exposure
prompt: A phone is splashed with liquid and immediately begins behaving erratically. What is the best immediate action?

options.text: Disconnect charging, power it off if safe, and follow the manufacturer liquid-exposure service guidance
Apply intense direct heat while leaving the phone running
Keep pressing buttons until it returns to normal
Connect a high-power charger to dry the port

explanation: Stop use and charging after liquid exposure and follow the manufacturer service guidance. Applying power or intense heat can worsen damage. Erratic operation is not a reason to continue stressing the device.

title: Isolate a VGA color problem
prompt: A legacy monitor displays a green color cast from one PC. Its internal color test is normal, and a verified replacement VGA cable restores correct colors. What is the most likely fault?

options.text: A permanent GPU failure despite operation with the replacement cable
The monitor panel regardless of the successful internal test
A source color profile despite the cable-only substitution restoring colors
The original VGA cable or its signal contacts

explanation: The cable substitution and normal internal display test isolate the issue to the original analog video path. A defective conductor or contact can affect a color channel. DHCP and printer profiles do not control that VGA signal.

title: Service a laptop storage bay
prompt: A service manual identifies a replaceable 2.5-inch SATA SSD held in a proprietary carrier. Which TWO items should the technician check before fitting the replacement?

options.text: Ignore the carrier height because capacity is the only compatibility requirement
Choose a SAS-only drive solely because it has a similar form factor
The replacement uses the SATA interface required by the bay
The bay and carrier support the replacement drive thickness
Assume a bare M.2 module fits without a supported carrier or adapter

explanation: Match both the physical bay/carrier dimensions and electrical interface. A drive form factor does not by itself prove interface compatibility. An M.2 module or display connection is not a direct substitute for this SATA bay.

title: Extend instead of duplicating the desktop
prompt: A user needs a presentation on one screen and private notes on another. Both displays work but show identical content. Which display mode should be selected?

options.text: Change only the audio output device
Extend the desktop across the displays
Duplicate the same desktop on both displays
Disable the secondary display

explanation: Extended desktop provides separate desktop space for the presentation and notes. Duplicate mode deliberately shows the same content. Disabling a screen or changing audio does not provide the required two-screen arrangement.
